text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Slovak parliament meets for its 20th session today. The agenda includes a controversial amendment to the securities law, giving the majority shareholder in a publicly traded issue the right to cancel trading in the share on the stock exchange.
- Parliament is also expected to discuss a law on protection of non-smokers, which would prohibit smoking in public places, such as bus stops.
- Germany's Volkswagen is the largest single foreign investor in Slovakia. It has invested 215 million marks in its plant in the capital of Bratislava since 1991.

- SEZ Dolny Kubin, Slovakia's major producer of electric insulation materals, said it planned to invest around 150 million crowns in modernisation over the next two years. SEZ expects turnover of around 250 million crowns this year, and said turnover should at least double within two years.

PRAVDA - Jozef Stranak, a parliamentarian for the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), who drafted the controversial amendment to a securities law, said he was willing to accept a compromise and delete the part that would give the majority shareholder in a publicly trade issue the right to cancel public trading in the share.
SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - Slovakia and South Africa are negotiating a visa-free travel agreement.
SME - Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said that accession talks with EU associate members - Hungary and Slovakia - should start at the same time.
